Title: Old English Core Vocabulary
Description: List of list c. 600 Old English literary core vocabulary words. Created by Christine Rauer (University of St Andrews).

Title: Old English Core Vocabulary St Andrews Flashcards
Description: Digital flashcards of OE core vocabulary with free access on Quizlet.Created by Christine Rauer (University of St Andrews).

Title: Old English Grammar Bytes
Description: Bite-size videos on Old English grammar, specifically cases, adjectives, verbs and nouns. Created by Thijs Porck (Leiden University)

Title: Old English Martyrology: An Annotated Bibliography
Description: Bibliography of publications on the Old English Martyrology. Created by Christine Rauer (University of St Andrews).

Title: Teachers of Old English in Britain and Ireland (TOEBI)
Description: A society for everyone involved in teaching Old English in Britain and Ireland. TOEBI organizes annual conferences and publishes a newsletter.

Title: Electronic Beowulf
Description: Electronic Beowulf is a digital edition of Beowulf closely based on its unique manuscript in British Library MS Cotton Vitellius A xv. The edition provides access to the poem and strategies for studying it in ways unavailable to print editions. The fifth edition allows scholars, students, and general readers, each with different interests and requirements, to customize the edition with ease. Created by Kevin Kiernan and Emi Iacob

Title: Essentials of Old English
Description: Manual of OE grammar with exercises, devided into Orthography and Pronunciation, Syntax, and Paradigms. Designed for beginners of OE with previous knowledge of basic PDE grammar and phonetics. An app version is also available. Created by the University of Glasgow.

Title: Nū ġē lā! A Pictorial Invitation to Old English
Description: Teaching manual with a selection of sentences from Ælfric's Grammar paired with present-day photographs. Created by Fritz Stieleke (Heinrich-Heine-Universität).

Title: Old English Core Vocabulary
Description: List of c. 600 OE literary core vocabulary words. Created by Christine Rauer (University of St Andrews).

Title: Old English Core Vocabulary St Andrews Flashcards
Description: Digital flashcards of OE core vocabulary with free access on Quizlet. Created by Christine Rauer (University of St Andrews).

Title: Old English Grammar
Description: Digital companion to Murray McGillivray’s Gentle Introduction to Old English with hypertext versions of the book’s texts, interactive grammar exercises, and outlines of OE grammar. Created by Murray McGillivray.

Title: Old English grammar exercises at ASNC Spoken Word
Description: Beginner and advanced OE grammar and translation exercises. Created by the University of Cambridge.

Title: Old English Online
Description: Website designed to help users learn to read Old English. Each module covers a major grammar concept and is accompanied by interactive exercises (vocabulary flashcards, fill-in-the-blank grammar quizzes with tailored explanatory feedback, reading comprehensions with optional glosses, notes, and translations). Created by Tom Birkett with Victoria Koivisto-Kokko (University College Cork).

Title: Old English Aerobics
Description: Anthology, Glossary and Workout Room. Supplementary materials to Peter S. Baker's Introduction to Old English, with online versions of all the texts in the book’s anthology, interactive exercises, and a glossary. Created by the University of Virginia.

Title: Playing with Old English: a Playful Pedagogy Resource
Description: Booklet with OE classroom activities, including instructions and printable materials, handouts, worksheets, slides. Designed within the framework of play pedagogy. Created by Megan Cavell and Renée Trilling (University of Illinois and University of Birmingham).

Title: ROEP: Resources for Old English Prose
Description: Resources for OE prose texts designed to aid researchers, instructors, and scholars at all stages. The website provides short introductions with bibliographies, translations, videos, and audio recordings, accompanied by images of the artefacts and manuscripts.Created by Francis Leneghan and Niamh Kehoe (University of Oxford).

Title: Teaching Old English in Schools
Description: Pedagogical resources for History and English teachers designed for classroom use, including worksheets and flashcards. Created by Fran Allfrey, Beth Walley, Carl Kears (King’s College, London).

Title: Wordwynn: Wynsum weġ tō ealdum Englisce
Description: Textbook of basic OE grammar and vocabulary focusing on OE as a medium of everyday communication, with audio files of the lesson texts. Designed for self-learners and beginner students Created by Fritz Stieleke (Heinrich-Heine-Universität).

Title: Bosworth-Toller Anglo-Saxon Dictionary
Description: Online edition of An Anglo-Saxon Dictionary, or a dictionary of "Old English." The project is based on a digital edition of An Anglo-Saxon dictionary, based on the manuscript collections of the late Joseph Bosworth (the so called Main Volume, first edition 1898) and its Supplement (first edition 1921), edited by Joseph Bosworth and T. Northcote Toller, today the largest complete dictionary of Old English. Maintained by Ondrej Tichy and Martin Rocek (Charles University of Prague).

Title: Germanic Lexicon Project
Description: Collection of digitized texts related to the early Germanic languages, with scanned image files. Includes A Concise Anglo-Saxon Dictionary by John R. Clark Hall (1916) and An Anglo-Saxon Reader by James W. Bright (1912). Parts of the work on An Anglo-Saxon Dictionary by Joseph Bosworth and T. Northcote Toller (1898 and 1921) later became the Bosworth-Toller Anglo-Saxon Dictionary. Created by Sean Crist.

Title: Dictionary of Old English website
Description: Dictionary of Old English, based on a computerized Corpus comprising at least one copy of each text surviving in OE and providing parsed lists of all attested spellings, grammatical information, and detailed sense divisions (supported by illustrative citations from the Corpus) for each word. Maintained by an International Advisory Board with members from Canada, Great Britain, the United States, and Germany, with worldwide contributions from expert scholars. Subscription is required for access.

Title: Online Etymology Dictionary
Description: Accounts of the origin and history of English words, compiled from old dictionaries and researched from archives available online. Not designed for linguistic research.

Title: A Thesaurus of Old English
Description: Conceptually arranged thesaurus of the vocabulary of Anglo-Saxon England. Within ordered categories, it provides information about word meaning resembling an inside-out dictionary (first the meanings and then the words). Created by the University of Glasgow.

Title: Beowulf on steorarume
Description: Digital edition of Beowulf with a PDE translation along the original OE text, with supplementary texts and PDE translations of The Fight at Finnsburh, Waldere, DeorWoden's Nine Herbs Charm, and Bede's Account of Cædmon. The website provides explanatory notes on the text and audio recordings in OE of selected passages. Created by Benjamin Slade.

Title: Electronic Beowulf 4.0
Description: Digital edition of Beowulf closely based on the original text.with images of all the early transcripts and collations of the manuscript. The edition restores original text through ultraviolet images and digitized backlighting to reveal erased or faded readings and the use of chemical reagents.Created by Kevin Kiernan, editor and designer, and Emil Iacob, software engineer (University of Kentucky, Georgia Southern University).

Title: Old English Poetry in Facsimile
Description: Created by Martin Foys with Kyle Smith and contributing editors (Digital Mappa)

Title: The Riddle Ages: Early Medieval Riddles, Translations and Commentaries
Description: Created by Megan Cavell with Matthias Ammon, Neville Mogford, Jennifer Neville, Alexandra Reider and Victoria Symons (University of Birmingham).

Title: Free, Fully Digitized Manuscripts Containing Old English
Description: Overview by Damian Fleming (Purdue University Fort Wayne).

The Corpus of Anglo-Saxon Stone Sculpture
Description: The Corpus identifies, records, and publishes English sculpture dating from the 7th to the 11th centuries, ranging from free-standing carved crosses and decorative elements to grave-markers.
